_comment: Atlas Growth UK :: SECOND RECOVERY pass over excluded_officp.csv — the UNRATED track. Sibling of recover-generic-uk-config.json, added 2026-09-16 at GATE 3 (proposal P7, operator-approved 'Apply all'). It reverses exactly one accident: a Maps listing with NO review data at all was being deleted by a review FLOOR that was never meant to judge it. Deterministic, $0, no re-scrape. Run AFTER the generic recovery: qualify-leads.js --in <run>/excluded_officp.csv --config recover-unrated-uk-config.json --out <run>/recover-unrated, then append recover-unrated/leads_clean_qualified.csv to the main qualified list (dedupe on place_id, assert zero overlap against BOTH the main pass and the generic recovery).
_r_the_bug: MEASURED, not remembered (3-row probe CSV through skills/google-maps-scrape/qualify-leads.js, 2026-09-16, output pasted in <run>/dryrun2-results.md): a BLANK review_count fails `review_count >= 5` IDENTICALLY to a 0. qualify-leads.js:92 does `const a=num(raw); if(a==null) return false;` and num('') is parseFloat('') = NaN -> null, so the comparison is never reached and the row is dropped `too_small`. Probe result: `>= 5` KEPT only the 5-review row and dropped BOTH the blank and the 0 row. That is 417 of the 1,114 too_small rows in this run — 107 of them UK, ICP-named and carrying a live website (Specialist Structural Waterproofing Ltd, Octopus Waterproofing Ltd, London Damp Proofing & Timber Treatment, Structural Waterproofing Services Wembley, GO5 LTD, National Waterproofing Group, Damp Proofing Staffordshire, Gunite Waterproofing, Rhino Damp Proofing). They are not ghosts; they are new or unreviewed listings. The 1-4 band is a different population and STAYS dropped — that band IS the ghost filter and the GATE 3 audit confirmed it is working (duplicate/inactive pins).
_r_no_engine_change: Expressed entirely in config, per CLAUDE.md (job tuning lives in the client config, never in the engine). qualify-leads.js has no `or` operator, so `review_count >= 5 OR (blank AND website)` cannot be written as one rule — it is written as a SECOND PASS whose rules are all ANDed instead. The engine already has everything needed: `not_exists` is a non-empty-trimmed-string test (qualify-leads.js:85-86) and it works on review_count exactly as on any other column. Probe, same 3-row CSV: `not_exists` on review_count KEPT only the blank row (dropped the 0 and the 5); `exists` kept the 0 and the 5 and dropped the blank; `in [""]` behaved identically to not_exists. `not_exists` is used here because it states the intent without depending on an empty string surviving a round-trip through the CSV writer.
_r_why_no_entity_rules: This pass does NOT repeat rules 1-4 of atlas-growth-uk-config.json, and that is a correctness argument from the engine, not an economy. qualify-leads.js:107 breaks on the FIRST failing rule (`for(const rule of active){ if(!passes(r,rule)){ reason=rule.label; break; } }`) and writes that rule's label as drop_reason. The review floor is rule 5 — the LAST rule — so a row carrying drop_reason 'too_small' is by construction a row that ALREADY PASSED rules 1-4: the hard entity deny, the primary-type deny, the name deny and the positive ICP allow. Re-applying them here could only produce the same verdict. This also means the pass inherits P1-P4 automatically: because it reads the excluded_officp.csv written by the CURRENT main config, a Rentokil branch primaried 'Water damage restoration service' with no reviews arrives here labelled too_small only once P1 has stopped dropping it at rule 2.
_r_track_marker: The recovery output carries no track column and one cannot be added downstream: PIPELINE.md STEP 3's append snippet deliberately writes every appended row through the MAIN file's header (that is how it strips qualify-leads.js's trailing drop_reason column), so any extra column would be dropped on append, and widening the main header would change the spine that footprint-gate.js / dedupe-ref.js / collapse-domains.js all read. No marker is needed: rule 1 admits ONLY rows whose review_count is empty, so every row this pass contributes is identifiable in the merged list by `review_count == ''` — an intrinsic, unspoofable marker. The 2,270-row merged list of the first pass contained no blank-review rows at all (they had all been dropped as too_small), so after the merge, blank review_count == recovered-unrated, exactly.

qualify_rules._r: 0. RECOVERY SCOPE GATE — same discipline as the generic recovery's rule 0, one drop reason only. Here it is 'too_small', so this pass can never re-litigate a deny: a row removed as hard_off_icp_type / off_icp_primary / name_deny / not_in_icp is refused before any other rule is read. CAVEAT (identical to the generic recovery): pointed at a file with NO drop_reason column, qualify-leads.js skips this rule with a WARN on stderr and the pass silently degrades to 'every unrated row with a website', which would readmit charities, bodyshops and builders merchants wholesale. Read the WARN line.
qualify_rules.label: not_an_unrated_candidate

qualify_rules._r: 1. UNRATED ONLY. Keeps the blank band and nothing else — the 1-4 band stays dropped here with label has_review_count, because those rows were judged on real review data and the floor's verdict on them stands. This is the rule that makes the pass safe to run over the whole too_small bucket.
qualify_rules.label: has_review_count

qualify_rules._r: 2. A LIVE WEBSITE is the substitute signal. With no reviews there is no activity evidence at all, so the pass demands the one other thing a ghost pin does not have. Note this is the ONLY place in the whole Atlas Growth UK rule set that gates on website — the main config's _no_website_rule explains why it refuses to (no-website rows are the STEP 5d recovery track, not junk), and that stays true for every RATED row. It is applied here only because an unrated AND site-less listing carries zero evidence of being a going concern. collapse-domains.js still classifies these websites site/shared_host/none downstream as usual, so a Checkatrade- or Facebook-only unrated firm is admitted here and then routed to the no-website track there, which is the correct handling.
qualify_rules.label: no_website
